title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the boundary stratification of the Deligne–Mumford compactification of M_{g,ν}, indexed by dual graphs ('MD-graphes'). For a graph G, S(G) is its set of vertices (irreducible components). Each component α has a genus g_α and a set Î_α of special points: marked points plus branches of nodes. M_G is the stratum, Π_1 its fundamental groupoid, and SΠ M_G is the fundamental groupoid of a punctured tubular neighbourhood of the stratum.

On the previous page Grothendieck obtained (144), Π_1 M_G ≃ ∏_{α∈S} Π_1 M_{g_α, Î_α}, by passing to the minimal 'strict' normalisation G̃. Strict normalisation morphisms then become equivalences.

This page:
(i) He notes that the structure of SΠ M_G in terms of the M_{g_α, Î_α} remains to be made explicit (deferred to the next number). On the next page this is the extension of Π_1 M_G by Z^{A(G)}, generated by Dehn twists about the edges.
(ii) For an arbitrary, non-strict 'modulation/normalisation' morphism G → G', he writes a commutative square (numbered 146). The top arrow Π_1 M_G → Π_1 M_{G'} is identified, via the vertical equivalences, with a bottom arrow ∏_{α∈S} Π_1 M_{g_α, Î_α} → ∏_{α'∈S'} Π_1 M_{g'_{α'}, Î'_{α'}}. Here S' is identified with a subset of S and g'_α = g_α. The bottom arrow factors as:
  - projection onto the factors indexed by S', followed by
  - Ψ = ∏ of maps (147), Π_1 M_{g_α, Î_α} → Π_1 M_{g_α, Î'_α}, using Î'_α ⊂ Î_α.
This is exactly what happens for the maps on boundary strata induced by forgetting marked points with stabilisation: unstable components are dropped, surviving components keep their genus and lose special points.
(iii) Conclusion: knowing all general modulation morphisms reduces to knowing the point-forgetting maps (148), Π_1 M_{g,I} → Π_1 M_{g,I'} for I' ⊂ I.
(iv) A marginal note says the diagram comes from an analogous diagram at the level of the elementary modular multiplicities (stacks).

The page serves the programme stated on the next page: determine, by generators and relations, the groupoids π_1 M_{g,I} functorially in I, together with the extensions Sπ_1 M_G and the generalisation maps between them. This is the 'Teichmüller tower / Lego' programme of the Esquisse.
errors: The identification Π_1 M_G ≃ ∏ Π_1 M_{g_α, Î_α} only holds for the rigidified/'strict normalised' version of the stratum. The actual DM stratum is a quotient of ∏ M_{g_α, Î_α} by Aut(G), and its fundamental groupoid is an extension by Aut(G). Presumably Grothendieck's M_G is already the labelled version, but the page leaves this implicit.
Equation numbering: the square on this page duplicates (or should be) (146), since (145) is already used on the previous page.

The factorisation implicitly assumes that every component of G' comes from a component of G of the same genus, with special points forming a subset. This needs the identifications made when contracting unstable rational components, which the page does not spell out ('sans plus de précisions').

ideas.what: Reduction of the maps on fundamental groupoids of boundary strata, induced by general graph morphisms, to projections onto components composed with point-forgetting maps π_1 M_{g,I} → π_1 M_{g,I'}
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality of the Teichmüller tower under forgetful maps; Birman-type forgetful homomorphisms between mapping class groups of components
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984), developed by Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura, Bakalov–Kirillov and others in the 1990s–2000s
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §2–3 (Teichmüller tower, structure at infinity of M_{g,ν}, operations of 'cutting' and forgetting points), in sketch form

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoid of a stratum as a product of fundamental groupoids of moduli of the components, via the normalised dual graph
ideas.modern_name: Boundary strata as products of M_{g_α, n_α} (modulo Aut of the dual graph); stabilisers of curve systems in the mapping class group

ideas.what: SΠ M_G as the extension of Π_1 M_G by Z^{edges}, generated by Dehn twists (announced here, made explicit on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental group of the punctured tubular neighbourhood of a boundary stratum (stabiliser of a multicurve)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; used e.g. by Nakamura and Boggi for tangential base points
ideas.where_published: Esquisse discusses 'structure à l'infini' only qualitatively

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine bookkeeping in Grothendieck's early working-out of the Teichmüller-tower programme. The reduction of graph-morphism functoriality to forgetful maps on components is standard and is essentially contained in the Esquisse and the later Lego literature. Its main interest is historical (the pre-Esquisse formalism of MD-graphs and 'modulation' morphisms), not new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: The bottom-left product should read ∏_{α∈S} Π_1 M_{g_α, Î_α}; the Π_1 is dropped in the transcription.
The square is most likely numbered (146), not (145), since (145) already appears on the previous page and the next equation is (147).
The lower node of the diagonal factorisation is ∏_{α'∈S'} M_{g_α, Î_α}. The diagonal arrow is the projection, labelled 'en identifiant S' à une partie de S, et g_α = g'_α'.
Margin: 'Ceci provient d'un diagramme analogue au niveau des multiplicités modulaires élémentaires...'. 'Multiplicités' is Grothendieck's term for orbifolds/stacks.
'+générale+' is an insertion above 'morphismes de modulation': 'la connaissance des morphismes de modulation générale se réduit à celle des morphismes (148)'.
